When this URL is reached through client-side navigation, topics#unsubscribe never runs, so notification settings remain unchanged even though the template says the user will stop receiving notifications. Ensure this route performs the unsubscribe operation (or forces navigation through the server endpoint) before displaying confirmation.

This confirmation promises that the user will stop receiving notifications for the topic, but unsubscribe sets watching/tracking topics to `regular`, not `muted`. Regular still permits notifications such as mentions and replies, so the message incorrectly tells those users they have stopped all topic notifications. Describe the reduction in notifications accurately (and distinguish regular from muted if necessary).

`TopicUser.find_by` can return nil for a logged-in user who has not visited this topic. Opening the new unsubscribe URL in that state raises NoMethodError at `tu.notification_level` rather than unsubscribing. Topic visibility does not guarantee a topic-user row exists (the visit updater explicitly creates missing rows). Initialize a missing row and apply the regular default notification level before choosing the new level.

issues.descricao: The new unsubscribe endpoint changes the user's topic notification level on a plain GET request, so a third-party page can trigger it for a logged-in user without any CSRF token.

comentarios.texto: The unsubscribe endpoint mutates notification_level (tu.save!) via a plain GET route (config/routes.rb:440-441) with skip_before_filter :check_xhr, authenticating only through the session cookie. There is no CSRF token (Rails forgery protection does not cover GET) and no capability token, unlike EmailController#unsubscribe which authorizes via DigestUnsubscribeKey. Any third-party page can embed and, when a logged-in user loads it, silently change that user's notification_level for the topic. Require a per-user capability token (like the digest unsubscribe key) in the URL, or perform the state change from an authenticated non-GET request that carries the CSRF token.

The new GET routes mutate the authenticated user's notification preferences without CSRF verification. An attacker can navigate a logged-in user's browser to a known topic unsubscribe URL and reduce or mute its notifications, because Rails excludes GET from forgery-token checks and unsubscribe explicitly skips check_xhr. Make GET render a confirmation page and perform the preference change through a CSRF-protected POST or PUT.

WHAT: The unsubscribe state change (lowering/muting notification_level + save!) runs on a GET route (config/routes.rb GET t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe). WHY: An attacker can forge the URL as an image/prefetch/link to silently change a victim's notification state with no CSRF token since GETs are not CSRF-protected. HOW: Make the mutation a PUT/POST with CSRF protection or require an explicit confirmation parameter/token instead of mutating on page view.

issues.descricao: TopicsController#unsubscribe dereferences TopicUser.find_by without handling a missing row, so users with no topic_users record get a NoMethodError/500 instead of being unsubscribed.
issues.textoGolden: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash

comentarios.texto: tu is not checked for nil before use. TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id]) returns nil whenever the logged-in user has no topic_users row for that topic (the same lookup TopicUser.get performs), and the next line dereferences tu.notification_level, raising NoMethodError and returning a 500. Because the route is only gated by ensure_logged_in, any logged-in user can hit /t/:topic_id/unsubscribe(.json) for a topic they never opened and trigger the crash. Guard the lookup, e.g. `tu = TopicUser.find_by(...); return render json: {success: false} unless tu` (or build/return early) before reading notification_level.

`TopicUser.find_by(...)` can return nil (e.g. the user clicks the emailed unsubscribe link for a topic for which no TopicUser row was ever created), and the very next line dereferences it (`tu.notification_level > ...`, then `tu.save!`). This raises NoMethodError on nil and the unsubscribe request 500s. Guard the nil case (e.g. return early or use `TopicUser.change`/`find_or_create_by`) before reading/writing notification_level.

`tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return nil (find_by yields nil when no row exists), but the next lines dereference it unconditionally (`tu.notification_level`, `tu.save!`). Since the new unsubscribe routes are public GET endpoints, any logged-in user visiting /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe for a topic they have never tracked will trigger a NoMethodError and a 500 instead of a sane response. Guard the nil case (e.g. create/skip or redirect) before reading notification_level.

issues.descricao: The message builder spec passes unsubscribe_url in the fixture but never asserts the per-topic unsubscribe link appears in the email.

comentarios.texto: The `unsubscribe_url` added to the `message_with_unsubscribe` fixture is never asserted. The two tests only check that the List-Unsubscribe header `be_present` and that the body matches `user_preferences_url`; neither references `unsubscribe_url`. So they would still pass if the topic-specific unsubscribe URL this PR introduces were dropped or wired to the wrong value. Add an assertion (e.g. that `message_with_unsubscribe.body` matches `/t/1234/unsubscribe`, and that the List-Unsubscribe header points at the topic unsubscribe URL) so the new behaviour is actually covered.

The fixture now passes unsubscribe_url, but no assertion reads it. The tests only check that the List-Unsubscribe header is present and that the body contains user_preferences_url, so they pass if the topic unsubscribe link is removed or broken. Add an assertion that the body includes "/t/1234/unsubscribe".

issues.descricao: The unsubscribe confirmation says the user will stop receiving notifications for the topic, but watching/tracking users are only moved to regular, which still sends mention/reply notifications.

comentarios.texto: The confirmation promises that the user will stop receiving notifications for this topic, but TopicsController#unsubscribe sets watching/tracking users to regular, not muted. Regular still allows mention/reply notifications, so this confirmation (and the corresponding promise in the new email link text) overstates what clicking the link accomplished. Describe stopping notifications for every new post, or make the confirmation conditional on the resulting notification level so only muted users are told that all topic notifications have stopped.

issues.descricao: Unsubscribe saves the new notification level without setting notifications_reason_id, so auto-tracked topics are promoted back to tracking on the next read, undoing the unsubscribe.

comentarios.texto: Saving the notification level directly leaves notifications_reason_id unchanged instead of recording an explicit user choice. For automatically tracked topics with a null reason, TopicUser.update_last_read promotes the row back to tracking when the reading threshold is exceeded, undoing the unsubscribe on the next read. Persist the change through TopicUser.change so notifications_reason_id and notifications_changed_at are set consistently with set_notifications.

Saving the notification level directly bypasses the explicit-user-change metadata set by TopicUser.change. In particular, a topic_user with notifications_reason_id == nil remains eligible for TopicUser.auto_track, which checks that field and can promote the topic back to tracking after the user unsubscribes. Use the notification-change helper (or set its user-change reason and timestamp consistently) so the unsubscribe is retained as an explicit user preference.

issues.descricao: Claims the client unsubscribe route never performs the unsubscribe when entered through an in-app transition.

comentarios.texto: The client unsubscribe route only loads the ordinary topic view and never performs the unsubscribe operation. When entered through an in-app transition rather than a full server navigation, PostStream.loadTopicView requests /t/:id.json (or consumes preload data), so the page claims notifications will stop while the persisted notification level remains unchanged. Ensure this entry path executes the unsubscribe operation before showing confirmation.

The client route loads the topic but never invokes the unsubscribe action. Notification levels are changed only by TopicsController#unsubscribe, so navigating to this route inside the Ember application can display “You will stop receiving notifications” without changing the subscription. Explicitly perform the unsubscribe operation on client-side entry rather than relying on the initial HTML request to have done it.

issues.descricao: The property name stopNotificiationsText is misspelled (should be stopNotificationsText).
issues.textoGolden: Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')

sugestoes.texto: The new cancellation requests use `client` without setting its API key in this cron module. `sgMail.setApiKey(sendgridAPIKey)` configures a separate internal client, so the standalone cron endpoint sends unauthenticated cancellation requests and cancelled bookings' emails remain scheduled. Initialize `client` with the SendGrid API key before issuing these requests.

Successful cancellations are not deleted from the database until every SendGrid request in the loop succeeds. If a later request fails, all earlier successful cancellations remain queued, and the next run POSTs those already-cancelled batches again; SendGrid rejects duplicate cancellations with 400, aborting the loop before remaining reminders can be cancelled. Await each reminder's database deletion immediately after its successful cancellation and handle failures per reminder so one rejected batch does not block the others.

The immediateDelete branch cancels the SendGrid batch and returns without deleting the reminder or setting cancelled. handleNewBooking now uses this branch for the original rescheduled booking but does not remove its reminder rows. Those rows therefore remain outside the cron cleanup query (which requires cancelled: true), unlike reminders cancelled through the normal branch. Delete the reminder after successful immediate cancellation, or mark it cancelled so it can be cleaned up.

This consumer replaces reminders after a workflow step is edited, but the new default deleteScheduledEmailReminder behavior only marks an existing scheduled email as cancelled. Previously it cancelled the provider batch immediately. The replacement email is scheduled while the old batch remains active until the cancellation cron runs, so an old reminder due before that run can still be delivered (potentially alongside its replacement). Use immediate cancellation for this replacement path, as the deleted-step path already does, and await it before scheduling replacements.

These Prisma deletes are lazy and run only after the entire external-request loop succeeds. If a cancellation request fails partway through (for example, an expired or invalid batch ID), execution jumps to the outer catch: none of the successfully cancelled rows are deleted, and no later reminders are cancelled. Since the failed row remains eligible without a lower date bound, it can repeatedly block the batch, allowing cancelled bookings' later emails to be sent. Handle failures per reminder and persist each successful cancellation independently so one bad batch cannot prevent progress on other reminders.

issues.descricao: Reminder cancel helpers are called without await inside forEach when bookings are cancelled/rescheduled or workflows edited, so the handler can return before reminders are cancelled or deleted and failures are unobserved.
issues.textoGolden: Asynchronous functions deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called without await inside forEach loops. This occurs during booking rescheduling/cancellation, and workflow/workflow step deletion/updates. Consequently, scheduled workflow reminders may not be reliably cancelled, potentially leaving them active.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder called inside forEach without collecting/awaiting promises. WHY: handler returns before cancels complete and rejections are unobserved, so cancellations are lost and reminder emails/SMS are still sent (same fire-and-forget pattern repeated in handleNewBooking:966, bookings.tsx:488, workflows.tsx:212/376/519/574).

Cancellation now delegates the database update/deletion to asynchronous reminder helpers without awaiting them, while removing reminder deletes from the awaited promise list. The handler can finish before cancelled flags or unscheduled-reminder deletions are persisted, allowing a subsequent scheduler run to schedule a cancelled booking's reminder and leaving cancellation work unfinished when a serverless invocation terminates. Collect and await the helper promises; apply the same correction to the modified rescheduling and workflow-update callers that discard these promises.

Await the reminder cancellation promises before completing the cancellation request. These helpers now own persistence of cancellation: email awaits a workflowReminder update and SMS awaits Twilio before deleting the row. The forEach discards their promises, and removing remindersToDelete from the awaited promise list removes the previous guarantee that reminder state is cleared before the handler returns. In a serverless request the outstanding operations can be interrupted after the response, leaving reminders active for a cancelled booking. Collect these helper promises and include them in the awaited Promise.all.

issues.descricao: The cron cancels SendGrid sends for cancelled reminders in one try around the whole loop, so one failing cancel aborts all remaining cancellations and the row deletions, and the failing row blocks later runs.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: remindersToCancel loop awaits SendGrid cancel per-reminder inside one try and only runs Prisma deletes after the loop, with no method filter. WHY: a single throw (e.g. null SMS referenceId sent as batch_id, or one SendGrid error) aborts the loop and skips Promise.all deletes, leaving all other cancelled emails still scheduled so they are still sent.

Successful cancellation records are only deleted after every SendGrid request in the loop succeeds. If a later request fails, the catch skips all queued Prisma deletions; the next run retries an already-cancelled batch, which SendGrid rejects with 400, and aborts before processing the remaining reminders. Await each reminder's database deletion immediately after its successful cancellation and isolate errors per reminder so one failed batch does not block the others.

Handle cancellation failures per reminder rather than around the entire batch. If one SendGrid request rejects (for example, for an expired or invalid batch ID), the loop exits before cancelling the remaining reminders, and Promise.all is never reached, so even earlier successfully cancelled reminders remain in the database. The failed record stays eligible for the next run and can repeatedly block other cancellations until their emails are sent. Execute each successful deletion and isolate failures so the worker continues processing the remaining reminders.

issues.descricao: Email reminders for cancelled bookings are only flagged cancelled and cancelled in SendGrid by the cron later, so reminders close to their send time can still be delivered.

comentarios.texto: Deferred cancellation includes reminders less than ten minutes from their scheduled send time, when SendGrid no longer permits cancellation. A booking cancelled in that interval is only marked cancelled locally by deleteScheduledEmailReminder, and the cron's POST is rejected, so its email is still delivered. Process cancellation before SendGrid's ten-minute cutoff and explicitly handle cancellations that arrive after that deadline rather than relying on this cron query to stop delivery.

issues.descricao: The cron cancels SendGrid scheduled sends one at a time with sequential awaits, which is slower than batching.

comentarios.texto: The new cancel loop performs a sequentially awaited SendGrid HTTP request (`await client.request(...)`) for each reminder returned by an unbounded `findMany` (no `take`), then deletes them. WHY: this is O(N) serial network round-trips per cron run; if many reminders are cancelled at once (e.g. a bulk event-type disable or booking cancellation wave) the cron handler can block for a long time on serial SendGrid latency. HOW: fan the independent SendGrid cancel requests out with `Promise.all`, and/or bound the query with `take` plus pagination, then batch the DB deletes.

WHAT: SendGrid cancel issued with sequential await inside for loop over remindersToCancel. WHY: cron blocks O(N) sequential network round-trips instead of parallel batch, materially slowing the hourly schedule job as cancelled backlog grows.

issues.descricao: deleteScheduledEmailReminder and its immediateDelete flag do not delete anything; the names no longer describe the behaviour.

comentarios.texto: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and its `immediateDelete` flag no longer match what the code does. The default path only marks the reminder `cancelled: true`, and the `immediateDelete` path only sends a cancel request to the email provider. Neither path deletes the scheduled send or the row, unlike the SMS counterpart, which still deletes. Rename them (for example `cancelScheduledEmailReminder` and `immediateCancel`) or document the behaviour.

issues.descricao: deleteScheduledSMSReminder deletes the DB row only after a successful Twilio cancel, so a cancel failure leaves the reminder row behind now that callers no longer delete it.

comentarios.texto: twilio.cancelSMS and prisma.workflowReminder.delete share one try block. If the Twilio cancel throws, the DB row is never deleted. The reminder row then stays behind for a booking that was cancelled, rescheduled or deleted, because the callers no longer delete rows themselves. Delete the row in a finally block, or handle the cancel failure separately so the delete still runs.

issues.descricao: Prisma is imported in workflows.tsx but no longer used.

comentarios.texto: `Prisma` is imported as a value (line 9) but is no longer used anywhere in this file. This PR removed the only usages (`Prisma.BatchPayload` in the now-deleted `remindersToDelete` / `deleteReminderPromise` declarations), while the import was kept. WHY: the repo's ESLint `no-unused-vars` rule will fail CI/build for an unused import. HOW: remove `Prisma` from the import list (and keep `import type { PrismaPromise }` as a type-only import).

sugestoes.texto: The denial-cache key concatenates name and parent with an unescaped underscore, so distinct resource checks share entries. For example, name `a_b` with parent `c` and name `a` with parent `b_c` produce the same key, allowing a denied check to incorrectly deny an authorized resource until expiry. Encode the components as an unambiguous tuple, such as a JSON array.

An error checking the cached permission snapshot returns immediately instead of attempting the fresh-permission fallback. When an outdated snapshot lacks a newly granted direct resource permission, checkPermission can enter checkInheritedPermissions and fail while loading the folder tree; the request then fails even though fresh direct permissions would authorize it without any folder lookup. Treat this cached-check error as a reason to fall through to getIdentityPermissions, and only return an error if checking the fresh permissions fails.

The test says it allows access to prove permissions are not checked, but seeds `"dashboards:uid:dash1": false`. Consequently, bypassing the explicit denial cache can still return false through the normal permission-check/fallback path, satisfying the assertion without exercising denial-cache precedence. Seed this scope as true so removing the denial-cache lookup makes the test fail.

The denial key does not uniquely encode the resource name and parent folder. For the same namespace, user and action, Name="a_b", ParentFolder="c" and Name="a", ParentFolder="b_c" both produce the suffix "_a_b_c". A denied check for the first resource therefore populates a denial for the second resource too; Check returns false directly on that cache hit without consulting its actual permissions. Encode the components unambiguously (for example as a JSON array or with length prefixes) so a cached denial cannot contaminate another resource's authorization result.

The underscore-delimited name and parent fields are ambiguous: a check for name `a_b` in parent `c` produces the same key as name `a` in parent `b_c` for the same namespace, user and action. If the first check is denied, the second returns false immediately from the denial cache without evaluating its permissions, even if access should be allowed. Encode the fields unambiguously (for example as a JSON array or length-prefixed tuple) rather than concatenating unrestricted identifiers with underscores.

issues.descricao: The denial cache key joins name and parent folder with underscores, so different name/parent pairs can collide and a cached denial for one resource denies another until TTL expiry.
issues.textoGolden: The cache key construction in `userPermDenialCacheKey` uses simple string concatenation with underscores, which can lead to ambiguous keys and collision risks when any component contains underscores or is empty. This could result in incorrect denial cache hits, affecting user permissions.

comentarios.texto: The denial cache key does not distinguish underscores inside resource and parent UIDs from its field separators. For the same namespace, user and action, (name="a_b", parent="c") and (name="a", parent="b_c") generate the same key, so denying the first request makes Check return false for the second even if its permissions explicitly allow it. Encode the components unambiguously, for example as a JSON tuple or length-prefixed fields.

The denial cache key is not injective: for the same namespace, user and action, `(name="a_b", parent="c")` and `(name="a", parent="b_c")` produce the same key. After the first request stores a denial, Check's new early cache return denies the second request without checking its permissions, even if it is allowed. Encode the components unambiguously (for example a JSON tuple or length-prefixed components) and add a test verifying that these two requests do not share a denial entry.

Make the denial-cache key encode component boundaries unambiguously (for example, length-prefix or serialize the components). For the same namespace, user and action, name `a_b` with parent `c` and name `a` with parent `b_c` both produce the suffix `_a_b_c`. Underscores can occur in resource UIDs, so denying the first request caches a key that causes Check to immediately deny the second request without evaluating its permissions, even if that resource is allowed.

issues.descricao: The explicit denial-cache test seeds the cached permission as false instead of true, so it would pass without the denial-cache short-circuit and does not verify it.
issues.textoGolden: The test comment says the cached permissions 'allow access', but the map stores false for dashboards:uid:dash1, so checkPermission will still treat this scope as not allowed.

comentarios.texto: This test claims to prove the permDenialCache short-circuit (service.go:116-121) denies access, but it seeds the cached permission as map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false} (a deny), contradicting its comment "Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked". Because the cached set is already a deny, checkPermission returns allowed=false, the code falls through to the DB path, and the fake store also returns no permissions, so Allowed stays false. The assertion passes even if the entire permDenialCache early-return were deleted. Seed the cached permission as true (map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": true}) so that only the denial-cache entry can force Allowed=false; otherwise the test does not verify the feature.

The comment says "Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked", but the code sets the permCache entry to `false`, which is a deny. The test therefore does not show that the permission cache is skipped. Set the value to `true`, or change the comment to match.

The 'Should deny on explicit cache deny entry' test would still pass if the permDenialCache check were removed. permCache is seeded with dash1:false, not true as the comment claims, so the normal path also denies. Seed permCache with {"dashboards:uid:dash1": true} and a store that grants the permission, so Allowed=false can only come from the denial entry.

issues.descricao: A cached permission set that denies a resource always triggers a full DB permission reload, so checks over many inaccessible dashboards issue one query per resource instead of being served from cache.

comentarios.texto: Every distinct resource denied by the cached permission map triggers a reload of the entire user's action permission set, because the denial cache is resource-specific and a cached false result always falls through to getIdentityPermissions. Sequential checks of N inaccessible dashboards therefore execute N full permission queries and cache rewrites even with a current action-wide cache; getUserPermissions' singleflight only merges overlapping requests. Bound refreshes per user/action with a short refresh cooldown or generation marker so different resource misses can share a recent refresh.

issues.descricao: The Service struct comment listing its caches was not updated for the new permDenialCache field.

comentarios.texto: The struct doc comment still reads "// Cache for user permissions, user team memberships and user basic roles", but this PR added the new `permDenialCache` field (line 58). The comment no longer enumerates what the struct actually holds and misleads a reader about the new denial-cache field; update it to mention the permission-denial cache so the prose matches the fields.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: Fallback locales are explicitly loaded only in the controller callback, leaving background translations without their fallback files. WHY: Jobs::Base sets I18n.locale and executes jobs without this callback, and translate_accelerator loads only config.locale; on a fresh worker using a non-English site locale, missing keys cannot fall back to English because backend fallback calls bypass the accelerator. HOW: Ensure the full fallback list is loaded at the shared translation entry point rather than relying exclusively on the HTTP controller callback.

WHAT: The fallback result now depends on SiteSetting.default_locale, but the shared accelerator cache does not include that setting or the current site in its key. WHY: translate_accelerator caches no-argument translations by key, current locale and backend identity only, so multisite requests using the same user locale but different site defaults reuse the first site's fallback text; changing the default locale also leaves cached fallback text stale. HOW: Include the effective fallback chain in the translation cache key so cached results are isolated by fallback configuration.

issues.descricao: Fallback locale catalogs are only loaded in the controller's set_locale filter, while translate loads just the current locale, so translations outside requests (jobs, mailers) cannot fall back to the site default or English.

comentarios.texto: Fallback catalogs are ensured loaded only in the controller filter, leaving non-controller translation paths without the catalogs required by the newly enabled fallback backend. Jobs::Base sets I18n.locale directly and PostAlerter uses I18n.with_locale, while the accelerator loads only the current locale and backend fallback lookups bypass that loader; missing keys therefore still produce missing translations or skip the configured site fallback until another request happens to load those catalogs. Ensure the full fallback chain is loaded at the translation boundary, rather than relying solely on the controller filter.

The new fallbacks contract requires the fallback locales (site default and :en, from FallbackLocaleList#[]) to be loaded before Backend::Simple#translate is asked for them — Backend::Simple only returns already-loaded translations. This PR added I18n.ensure_loaded!/I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! but wired it only into ApplicationController#set_locale, and the loader that actually gates every translation, I18n.translate (line 68), still loads only `config.locale`. As a result, any I18n.t performed outside the request cycle (console, background jobs, mailers) or before set_locale runs will not load the fallback locales and will silently return 'translation missing' instead of the fallback the new I18n.fallbacks advertises. Fix: have translate ensure the fallback chain is loaded (e.g. call I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! / load the fallback locales here), not rely on the controller hook.

translate loads only config.locale, but the new fallback chain (default_locale, :en) is loaded only by the controller's I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!. Outside controllers (jobs, mailers, rake), a key missing in the current locale falls back to a locale that is not loaded, so it returns 'translation missing', and the LRU cache then stores that result. Fix: in translate, call I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! (or load each locale in fallbacks[config.locale]) before the lookup.

issues.descricao: The translation cache key does not include the site or its default locale, but fallback results now depend on SiteSetting.default_locale, so multisite processes or a changed default locale serve stale fallback translations.

comentarios.texto: The new fallback order depends on SiteSetting.default_locale, but the accelerator's translation cache does not include that setting or the current site in its key. In a multisite process, two sites with the same user locale and different default locales reuse the first site's cached fallback translation; changing the default locale also leaves cached fallback results stale. Include the effective fallback chain or site/default-locale context in the translation cache key.

sugestoes.texto: BuildIndex now leaves the cache unlocked throughout construction, so GetIndex can return nil for a key whose index is already being built. Concurrent Search calls or Search racing with handleEvent can therefore build separate indexes for the same key; the last cache assignment replaces the other index, potentially discarding updates written by the event handler, and repeats the full resource scan. Serialize builds per NamespacedResource and recheck the cache after acquiring that key's lock, while allowing different keys to build concurrently.

The new TotalDocs call iterates Bleve's cache without a read lock after the write-event consumer has already started. A write event for an uncached namespace can call getOrCreateIndex and publish an index while TotalDocs ranges over the map, causing a data race and potentially a fatal concurrent map iteration/write error during startup. Protect the cache iteration in bleveBackend.TotalDocs with cacheMu.RLock/RUnlock.

issues.descricao: BuildIndex now locks only the final cache assignment, so concurrent callers for the same uncached key all build the same expensive index in parallel and the last one overwrites the others.
issues.textoGolden: A race condition in BuildIndex allows multiple goroutines to concurrently build the same expensive index for the same key. This is caused by moving the b.cacheMu lock from protecting the entire function to only protecting the final cache assignment.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: Removing the function-wide `b.cacheMu.Lock()/defer Unlock()` and keeping only the lock around `b.cache[key]=idx` removes the only thing that serialized GetIndex against an in-flight build. WHY: getOrCreateIndex (resource/search.go:287-307) does GetIndex -> if nil -> build; previously BuildIndex held the write lock for its whole body so a concurrent caller's GetIndex (RLock) blocked until the first build cached the index and then saw it (no second build). Now GetIndex can return nil while a build for the same key is still running, so two requests/watch events build the SAME key concurrently — producing two distinct index instances where the caller holding the non-cached one never observes later writes (stale search results), and, for file-backed indices (size > FileThreshold), two concurrent `bleve.New(dir, mapper)` opening the same on-disk directory. HOW: guard the build per key (e.g. re-check the cache under the write lock after acquiring it, or use a per-key single-flight/lock so only one build runs per NamespacedResource), rather than relying on a global write lock held for the entire body.

The cache mutex was moved to cover only the cache assignment, removing the serialization that previously surrounded the whole BuildIndex. Two concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same key can now both construct an index (including `bleve.New(dir, mapper)` on the same on-disk path) and both write `b.cache[key]`; the second overwrites the first, so callers get distinct index instances for one key and writes made through the losing instance are invisible to readers of the cached one (and the file-backed build may collide on the same directory). Keep the build for a given key serialized (e.g. restore the lock around the build, or take a per-key lock) instead of locking only the map write.

Locking only cache publication allows concurrent requests for the same uncached key to build separate indexes and overwrite each other's cache entries. Search and handleEvent both call getOrCreateIndex, whose GetIndex previously blocked behind the build-wide lock; now an event can update one newly built index before another build replaces it, losing that update from subsequent search results and leaving the discarded index open. Serialize builds per NamespacedResource and recheck the cache after acquiring that per-key guard.

issues.descricao: The new startup log calls TotalDocs, which iterates the index cache without a lock, after the event goroutine that can add indexes has started, so a concurrent map read and write can crash the process.
issues.textoGolden: Calling s.search.TotalDocs() here may race with concurrent index creation: TotalDocs iterates b.cache without synchronization, and the event watcher goroutine started just above could trigger BuildIndex writes concurrently, potentially causing a concurrent map read/write panic.

comentarios.texto: The newly added `s.search.TotalDocs()` call is unsafe: `bleveBackend.TotalDocs()` (pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:144-150) iterates `b.cache` without holding `cacheMu`, while the bleve.go hunk in this same PR keeps `cacheMu` for the `b.cache[key] = idx` write only. Because search.go:207-213 already started the watch-event goroutine that can call `build` → `BuildIndex` → cache write, line 216 can iterate the map concurrently with that write, causing a `concurrent map iteration and map write` panic or data race. Either guard the `TotalDocs` read with `cacheMu`, or move this call to a point where no build can run concurrently.

The new startup log calls TotalDocs after launching the write-event listener, but bleveBackend.TotalDocs iterates b.cache without cacheMu.RLock. A write event for an unindexed resource can concurrently publish an index through BuildIndex, causing a map iteration/write race and potentially a fatal runtime error during initialization. Protect TotalDocs cache iteration with the same read lock used by GetIndex.

BuildIndex now writes b.cache under Lock while TotalDocs (called from search.init after the watch goroutine starts) ranges over b.cache without any lock. This can cause a concurrent map read/write fatal error. Fix by taking cacheMu.RLock in TotalDocs.

issues.descricao: NewResourceServer returns an error when Init fails without cancelling the server context created earlier.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: NewResourceServer now calls s.Init(ctx) and, on error, returns `nil, err` without invoking the `cancel` func created at line 229 and without running any lifecycle cleanup. WHY: Init may have already started long-lived goroutines — searchSupport.init's event-consumption loop uses context.Background() (resource/search.go:202) and initWatcher starts a watcher bound to s.ctx (server.go:752-770) — so if search.init succeeds and initWatcher (or a later step) fails, the constructor discards the server while those goroutines keep running with no way to stop them, leaking the internal context and watcher goroutines. HOW: on the error path call `cancel()` (and any needed lifecycle.Stop) before returning, or defer the cancel until success.

WHAT: NewResourceServer calls s.Init(ctx) synchronously but returns nil,err without calling the cancel created for s.ctx. WHY: Failed startup leaks the server context (and any lifecycle/watch resources partially started by Init), leaving goroutines/channel watches alive. HOW: On Init error call s.cancel() (and lifecycle Stop cleanup) before returning.

issues.descricao: In getBaseConditions, the branches for a missing authorization condition are unreachable because getAuthorizationConditions always returns a Prisma.Sql.
issues.textoGolden: In getBaseConditions(), the else if (filterConditions) and final else branches are unreachable. This is because getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql object, making authConditions always truthy, which means only the first two if/else if conditions are ever evaluated.

comentarios.texto: getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql, so the `else if (filterConditions)` and final `else` branches (returning NOTHING_CONDITION) in getBaseConditions can never execute. Simplify to: if filterConditions, combine it with authConditions; otherwise return authConditions.

Unreachable branches in getBaseConditions: authConditions is always a truthy Prisma.Sql object (never null, NOTHING is `1=0`), so `else if (filterConditions)` and final `else { return NOTHING }` can never execute. Simplify to if(filter) return auth AND filter else return auth, or make the nothing-case explicit.

WHAT: `getBaseConditions` returns `filterConditions` alone (no authorization predicate) when `authConditions` is falsy (`else if (filterConditions) { return filterConditions; }`). WHY: The WHERE clause returned to consumers then contains no ownership/authorization restriction, so a caller using it would return every booking matching the filters (e.g. all bookings for the given eventTypeId/memberUserId) regardless of the requesting user's org/team membership — an authorization-boundary bypass if `getAuthorizationConditions()` ever yields a falsy value. HOW: Always AND the authorization predicate with the filters and fall back to `NOTHING_CONDITION` when no auth predicate exists, e.g. `return filterConditions ? Prisma.sql`(${authConditions}) AND (${filterConditions})` : authConditions;` (or keep the `NOTHING_CONDITION` default when auth is missing).

issues.descricao: The getBaseConditions test uses a single booking matching both auth and filter conditions, so it would pass even if the conditions were not combined.

comentarios.texto: The rewritten "should combine authorization and filter conditions" test cannot fail if the combination is broken. The fixture creates a single booking that satisfies the auth condition (userId = user.id AND teamId IS NULL) and the filter condition (eventTypeId = eventType.id) independently, so getBaseConditions returning auth-only, filter-only, or the AND combination all yield the same single-row result asserted here. Only a `1=0` result would be caught. Make the data distinguish the two: add a booking that matches the filter but not the auth (e.g. a team booking with the same eventTypeId), then assert the result excludes it, so that dropping either branch changes the returned rows.

issues.descricao: GetWebAssets does not re-check the cache after acquiring the write lock, so concurrent callers that missed the cache each reload the assets manifest.
issues.textoGolden: The GetWebAssets function implements an incomplete double-checked locking pattern for caching web assets. The function first checks if the cache is populated using a read lock (RLock), and if the cache is empty, it acquires a write lock to populate it. However, it fails to re-check whether the cache was populated by another goroutine while waiting to acquire the write lock.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: The exclusive lock acquired at line 48 is held (via defer on line 49) across the blocking file read / synchronous CDN HTTP request (lines 56-67) and there is no re-check of entryPointAssetsCache after acquiring the lock. WHY: On a cold cache, all concurrent callers (api/index.go:82, api/frontendsettings.go:62, middleware/recovery.go:141) block on the write lock and then each sequentially re-executes the full load (file I/O or blocking http.DefaultClient.Do), producing a thundering-herd serialization and N redundant loads instead of one; in Dev mode this happens on every request since the fast path is skipped, serializing all concurrent page loads. HOW: after `entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock()` re-check the cache (`if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil { return entryPointAssetsCache, nil }`) so only the first goroutine performs the load, and drop the defer in favor of releasing the lock immediately after assigning `entryPointAssetsCache = result` to avoid holding it during I/O.
cache is not re-checked under the lock after re-acquiring write Lock, so concurrent callers can each recompute web assets

The cache is not rechecked after acquiring the write lock, so concurrent production requests that initially observe a nil cache each reload and decode the manifest even after another request has populated it. During a cold-start request burst, these redundant filesystem reads and JSON decodes execute serially under the global lock, delaying queued page and frontend-settings requests and blocking cache readers while each reload runs. After acquiring the write lock, return the populated cache when cfg.Env != setting.Dev before performing asset loading.

issues.descricao: get_failure_reason's docstring examples do not match the strings the function returns.

comentarios.texto: The `get_failure_reason` docstring describes output this function does not produce. The singular branch (line 146) returns a `SINGULAR_HUMAN_FAILURE_MAP` value such as "A missed check-in was detected", yet the docstring advertises "A failed check-in was detected"; the multi-check-in branch joins `"%(count)d %(status)s"` fragments with `get_text_list(..., last_word=_("and"))` and appends " check-ins detected", yielding "2 missed and 1 error check-ins detected", not the docstring's "2 missed check-ins, 1 timeout check-in and 1 error check-in were detected". Update the examples (or the format string) so the documented contract matches the code.

The get_failure_reason docstring examples don't match the output. It shows 'A failed check-in was detected' and '...were detected', but the code returns the per-status singular strings ('A missed check-in was detected') or '<list> check-ins detected'. Update the examples to the real output and fix the 'humam readible' typo.

issues.descricao: get_monitor_environment_context builds a config copy with the human-readable schedule_type but returns the original monitor.config, so the conversion is lost and the context shows the raw value.
issues.textoGolden: The function modifies the config variable to include display values but then returns the original monitor.config instead of the modified version.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: get_monitor_environment_context copies monitor.config to `config` and converts schedule_type display, but returns the original monitor_environment.monitor.config instead of `config`. WHY: the display conversion never takes effect so the occurrence context carries the raw schedule_type value, producing wrong output vs the function's evident intent. HOW: return `"config": config` instead of `"config": monitor_environment.monitor.config`.

Dead computation: `config` is copied and `config['schedule_type']` transformed to display value, but return uses `monitor_environment.monitor.config` (original) instead of `config`. Change to `"config": config` so transformation is used.

WHAT: In get_monitor_environment_context the code copies config and replaces config['schedule_type'] with the human-readable get_schedule_type_display(), but the returned context dict uses the original `monitor_environment.monitor.config` instead of the modified local `config`, so the mutation is dead. WHY: The occurrence's monitor context always reports the raw schedule_type value rather than the display string the code intended to substitute, producing incorrect evidence data in the emitted occurrence. HOW: return the local variable, i.e. use "config": config in the returned dict.
